title: Longest Palindrome by Concatenating Two Letter Words
summary: Given an array of strings where each string consists of two lowercase English letters, determine the maximum length of a palindrome that can be formed by concatenating some of these strings, with each string used at most once.
statement: Given an array of strings where each string consists of two lowercase English letters, determine the maximum length of a palindrome that can be formed by concatenating some of these strings, with each string used at most once. If it is impossible to form any palindrome, return 0.
constraints: Every word contains exactly two lowercase letters and each occurrence may be used once.
Arrange selected words in any order so the concatenation is a palindrome.
Return the maximum possible character length.
hints: Nonsymmetric words must pair with their reverse; symmetric words pair among themselves with at most one leftover center.
Count words, process one lexical orientation of each reverse pair, and track whether any symmetric odd count exists.
Add 4 per reverse pair or symmetric pair, then add 2 once for a center if available.
Mirrored blocks are necessary outside the center, and these independent maximum pairings can always be concatenated into a palindrome.

tests.explanation: lc and cl form mirrored ends while gg occupies the center, totaling six.
The reverse pairs ty/yt and lc/cl contribute eight characters; unmatched ab words cannot be used.
